text:
Alice M: heads-up — after the NCCL 2.26.3 rollout to ap-northeast yesterday we started seeing degraded allreduce throughput and intermittent hangs/timeouts in multi-gpu inference jobs. p95->p99 jump ~2-3x on our 8xA100 canaries.
Ben K: ugh. only in ap-northeast? or across zones? :eyes:
Alice M: mostly ap-northeast 1a/1b. small sample from a nightly infer job: shows allreduce tail latency spikes and then eventual NCCL timeouts. logs below.
Alice M: ```
[2026-03-17T22:03:12Z] NCCL WARN CONNECT : Timeout waiting for ring setup, src 0 dst 3
[2026-03-17T22:03:12Z] nccl: NCCL Allreduce failed: unhandled cuda error, aborting
[2026-03-17T22:03:13Z] jobid=inf-8345 state=FAILED reason=NCCL_TIMEOUT
```
Carla S: can you paste driver/kernel and the exact nccl package we rolled? also which topology (nvlink vs pcie)?
Alice M: stack: NCCL 2.26.3-rc1 (bumped in yesterday's infra rollout), NVIDIA driver 535.86, kernel 5.15.0-70-generic, nv_peer_mem loaded. nodes are mixed: majority NVLINK (DGX-like) but some PCIe racks too.
Dmitri V: let's repro with nccl-tests to isolate. run on 8 GPUs: `all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2 -g 8` and also `./build/all_reduce_perf -p0` (no ibverbs) to compare. If nvlink path shows high tail, it's likely an NCCL kernel/runtime regression.
Ben K: we saw a faint signal in us-west after the driver bump last week but it was transient. ap-northeast looks more consistent. recommend canary-rollback NCCL to 2.26.2 on 3 racks and run the perf test.
Alice M: repro output from a failing run (truncated):
```
# ./all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2 -g 8
root: iter 100/1000, avg=3.12ms, p99=14.2ms
root: iter 101/1000, allreduce hang detected, waiting for response
NCCL WARN CONNECT: connect timed out, peer 3
NCCL WARN: collective aborted, aborting
```
Carla S: also check rdma/ibverbs and switch firmware/drivers for NICs. we had an 'Unreachable remote CQE' backtrace in a similar event earlier.
Dmitri V: agree. also capture CUDA kernel dumps and nvpeer memory stats. can someone attach dmesg + nvidia-smi topo?
Alice M: attaching (pasted): `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows NVLINK between 0-1-2-3 and 4-5-6-7, but inter-plane connectivity uses PCIe bridges. dmesg shows repeated: `nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU 3: peer memory registration failed: -110`
Ben K: I'm going to spin up 3 canary racks on ap-northeast and rollback NCCL package there. runtime-bot, please mark impacted nodes and block autoscaler from shifting jobs onto them.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for package `nccl=2.26.2` on cans-apne-001..003.
runtime-bot: autoscaler flagged, locked 3 racks from scheduling at 2026-03-17T23:05Z.
Carla S: once rolled back, run the all_reduce_perf loop for 30 minutes and collect p50/p95/p99. if p99 drops to baseline, we can attribute to NCCL change. if not, escalate to kernel/driver.
Alice M: thanks — starting the canary now. cc @Ben K for extra GPUs, @Dmitri V for repro script. I'll post results in ~40m. :thumbsup:
Ben K: FYI I've opened a ticket with NVIDIA — sent logs and dmesg. reference NV-98734. they asked for kernel logs and the exact nccl commit id.
Dmitri V: if rollback fixes it, plan: hold NCCL 2.26.3 for stable fleets, run extended perf-suite across nvlink+pcie racks, then reattempt with updated ibverbs/rdma stack.
Alice M: can confirm after rollback on canaries p99 returned to normal (~baseline) and no timeouts in 45m run. collecting histograms and will propose we pin fleets to 2.26.2 until we can coordinate a combined kernel/ibv/NCCL rollout.
Carla S: +1. please include cost note — if we need extended canaries we might reserve extra capacity for the next 48h. ops: estimate added GPU-hours = ~180 GPU-hours.
Ben K: noted. I'll update the incident board and draft a short postmortem if we decide to keep the hold.
Alice M: thanks all. will update with the full perf artifacts and the NVIDIA ticket link when they respond.
